evals.prompt: Wire up email and password sign-in. Call signInWithEmailAndPassword in the browser, then post the ID token to /v1/auth/session to get the cookie.
evals.expected_output: Should make password sign-in server-first: the browser posts email and password to the API, which runs the lockout, checks the password through Identity Toolkit, writes the audit entry and answers a custom token the client signs in with. Signing in with the password in the browser skips the lockout and alerts. The session route accepts only a token whose auth_time is within five minutes, sets the httpOnly cookie, and the client SDK then signs out with in-memory persistence. Every credential failure answers the same.
expectations: Moves the password check to the API
Applies a lockout before checking the password
Returns a custom token for the client
Session minting requires a sign-in within five minutes
Client SDK holds no session after the exchange
Gives the same answer for wrong password and unknown address

evals.prompt: Implement sign-out. Just delete the session cookie in the response.
evals.expected_output: Should explain that clearing the cookie isn't signing out: a Firebase session cookie stays valid until it expires. Should end the session on the server — delete the session's record (each session has its own id and record) or, without session records, revoke the account's refresh tokens. The response sends `Clear-Site-Data: "cache", "storage"` but not `"cookies"`, which would also drop the device cookie.
expectations: States that clearing the cookie alone leaves it valid
Ends the session on the server
Sends Clear-Site-Data with cache and storage
Does not include cookies in Clear-Site-Data, and says why

evals.prompt: Product wants passwords to need an uppercase letter, a number and a symbol, minimum 8 characters, and to expire every 90 days. Add that to the signup schema.
evals.expected_output: Should push back with NIST SP 800-63B: no composition rules and no scheduled changes; at least 15 characters when the password is the only factor (8 only with a second factor), at least 64 allowed, every character including spaces and Unicode, never truncated. Should add a breached-password check (Have I Been Pwned's range API) at creation and again at sign-in. Should ask the person to confirm before deviating, and if the product insists, record the deviation in AGENTS.md with its reason rather than silently applying it.
expectations: Refuses composition rules and expiry, citing NIST
Allows at least 64 characters and doesn't truncate
Adds a breached-password check at creation and sign-in
Asks before deviating, or records the deviation with a reason

evals.prompt: Users can sign in with Google or with a password. A user who registered with a password tries Google with the same email and gets auth/account-exists-with-different-credential. Just create a new account for the Google sign-in.
evals.expected_output: Should refuse a second account: one account per email. Should ask the person to sign in the way they did before, then link Google to that account with linkWithCredential. Should guard against pre-hijacking — an unverified account never gains a linked provider; the email is verified first (Firebase drops an unverified password when Google signs in to its own addresses).
expectations: Refuses to create a second account
Links the provider after signing in the existing way
Requires a verified email before linking
